name: Copper Creek Dam failure, Larkspur Valley flood
summary: Invented drill fiction for the invented Juniper Plains Area in the Larkspur Valley: no real place, organization or person. Sunday 21 March, 07:50, daylight, +4 °C and light rain after three days of warm rain on a deep snowpack. Copper Creek Dam has been seeping since Saturday evening; the county orders Copper Ridge below the dam and the Copper Creek corridor through south Larkspur out, and warns the river bottoms and Alder Flat. Sacrament meetings are at 9:00: the Stake Presidents must decide to cancel. At T+38 the dam fails. The flood wave takes the Route 30 bridge at Copper Ridge (T+45), reaches south Larkspur at 09:00 (T+70: the Route 12 bridge over Copper Creek closed, the Larkspur Care Center surrounded by water), floods the Copper Creek substation and cuts the fibre under the Route 12 bridge (T+75 to T+78): cellular dies in the south and the stakes go to Contingency (radio). The river crests through Larkspur West and reaches Alder Flat (T+140). Care-facility residents with no transport, missionaries not accounted for, Spanish-speaking families, members with relatives, a dam rumour, unasked volunteers, Supply Orders to the welfare line and a storehouse truck from Bramble Junction, city requests by ICS 213RR (Incident Command System resource request), and a wet-snow night ahead. Acronyms: EOC (Emergency Operations Center), PACE (Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency), SITREP (situation report), ERD (Emergency Response Director), WSRM / AWSRM ((Area) Welfare and Self-Reliance Manager), NWS (National Weather Service), VARA (the Winlink radio mode), FRS / GMRS (Family / General Mobile Radio Service).

pace.why: Cellular is up but congested: one call in three fails and texts arrive late; data works.

The Copper Creek substation flooded at T+75 and the fibre under the Route 12 bridge was cut at T+78: cell sites in the south half are off the air. Two failed attempts in 15 minutes (T+72, T+78): the specialist recommended Contingency, the Stake President decided, the net announced it.
Internet works in the north half (home Wi-Fi, a business on Main Street) and the stake center has Starlink with a named operator; a round-trip test with the line above passed three times at T+170.
Portable cell sites on generators serve the north half; a second round-trip test passed. The south wards stay on what works for them.

phases.title: Order and warning
phases.narrative: Sunday morning, steady rain, the creek brown and loud. Deputies drive the streets below the dam with loudspeakers; cell broadcast alerts reach most phones but not all. Families in their church clothes load cars; others have not heard. The 9:00 meetings are an hour away. The care facility on the south side of Larkspur has 46 residents and one van. Two sister missionaries do not answer their phone. Phones still work, slowly: first reports arrive by the phone app.
phases.controller: Keep the pace calm but steady. Make sure the Stake President player hears the meetings question at T+3. Do not hint at the breach.

phases.title: Breach and flood wave
phases.narrative: At 08:28 the embankment goes. A wall of brown water takes the Route 30 bridge at Copper Ridge and cuts the town in two; the retirement village grounds flood to the windows. 911 rings out. At 09:00, when the meetings would have started, the water reaches south Larkspur: the Route 12 bridge closes, the care center is surrounded, the substation floods. Phones fail one by one in the south.
phases.controller: Read the breach note aloud at T+38. Hand the rooftop net card to the HAM player at T+47. At T+80 confirm the step down to Contingency was decided, not assumed.

phases.title: Contingency: radio and runners
phases.narrative: The south half of the valley is dark and silent except for radios. Reports come by Winlink VARA FM, by net cards and by a soaked runner. The river rises through Riverside and reaches Alder Flat. Warming centres fill; families with relatives across the valley are reported missing and then found; a rumour that a second dam failed sends cars onto Route 12; Winlink gateways congest; the repeater on Saddleback Peak runs down its battery; a donations truck and forty volunteers arrive unasked; the county shelter fills and asks for a meetinghouse.
phases.controller: If a Satellite EOC laptop is in the room, open it at T+57 with the wards south of Copper Creek and let it roll up to the Stake EOC.

phases.title: Holding through a cold, wet night
phases.narrative: Rain turns to wet snow. Internet returns in the north first; the stake steps up to Alternate after a round-trip test and to Primary for the north wards near the end. Supply Orders are approved and a truck leaves Bramble Junction by the long way round. Work Crew Logs come in from sandbag, moving and warming-centre crews; the first mud-out crews go into streets the county has reopened. The night plan and the 72-hour posture are written before the drill ends.
phases.controller: Do not let the players step up without the test card. End with the hot wash at T+236.

injects.text: 07:50 DRILL. Sunday morning, +4 °C, light rain after three days of warm rain on a deep snowpack. The Larkspur Valley Irrigation District reported seepage at Copper Creek Dam last evening; at 07:40 the wet area on the downstream face began carrying muddy water. Larkspur County Sheriff: evacuation ORDER (leave now) for Copper Ridge below Route 30 and the Copper Creek corridor through south Larkspur, south of 500 South from Route 12 to the river. Evacuation WARNING (get ready to leave) for the Larkspur River bottoms from Center Street to Alder Flat. Most members are getting ready for 9:00 sacrament meetings. This is a simulation.

07:52 National Weather Service (NWS): flash flood warning for Copper Creek below the dam and for the Larkspur River from Larkspur to Alder Flat until 16:00. The river gauge at Center Street reads 2.9 m and is rising; flood stage is 3.2 m.

Sacrament meetings start at 9:00. Families will drive toward meetinghouses in and near the order zone. Decide now, with {erd} and {specialist}: are the 9:00 meetings in the stake cancelled, which buildings stay closed, and how members are told (phone tree, ministering, text, the net). Record it as a work item with "meetings" in the title and the decision written in: who decided, which meetings, which channels, what minute.

need.label: Sunday meetings decided (cancelled or not, which buildings, which channels) and recorded within 20 minutes

injects.lesson: Kerr County 2025 and Valencia 2024: people were on the move toward the water because no one told them to stay away in time.

injects.text: The county alert went out by cell broadcast at 07:48. Older phones, phones on silent for church, visitors and many Spanish-speaking members will not have it. Recommend to the Stake President how members in the ORDER zone are told to leave now and members in the WARNING zone to get ready: which area, which action, which channels (phone tree, ministering brothers and sisters, block captains, door knocks, the net), in English and Spanish. The Stake President decides; {erd} or you announce it. Record it as a work item with "notify" in the title and the decision written in.

need.label: Member notification for the order and warning zones recommended, decided and announced (area, action, channels, languages) within 20 minutes

injects.lesson: Valencia 2024: the public alert came after most of the deaths; Kerr County 2025: no county alert reached many phones; the stake must reach its own members.

injects.text: Net control: 'This is {eoc_call} opening the {stake} emergency net on the Saddleback Peak repeater. The level is PRIMARY, cellular. This net is the backup and carries wards without signal. Stand by for roll call.'

07:58 Cellular is up but congested: about one call in three fails, texts arrive up to ten minutes late, data works. Members are calling bishops, bishops are calling the Stake President, everyone is calling 911.

injects.note: Every unit's first Disaster Report, sent by phone while cellular holds: who has left, who is still home, who cannot leave. Values by severity band.

injects.text: Net control: 'All {stake} stations, roll call by ward. Give your call, your ward, how many families in the order zone have left, and anyone who cannot leave without help.' (Operator: note every ward that does not answer.)

injects.note: The care-facility and retirement branches report: residents who cannot leave on their own, no transport of their own, a building in the order zone.
injects.lesson: Eaton 2025: wheelchair users died after three 911 calls while paratransit stood uncalled; night staff had no recall list; Noto 2024: six in ten deaths were aged 70 or over.

injects.title: Transport for the residents of {unit} out of the order zone: wheelchair users and oxygen; request through the county, headcount at departure and arrival
injects.detail: The facility has one van for six people. Wheelchair users and oxygen patients go by county or care-facility transport, never in members’ cars. Pull the unit’s list of members with special needs and give every name a ministering contact.
injects.next: Request transport through the county liaison; name the destination (a building outside the warning zone with power for oxygen concentrators); count heads at departure and at arrival; record the request minute, destination and headcount as the decision

need.label: Transport for the residents of the unit requested through the county within 30 minutes, destination and headcount recorded as the decision

injects.text: 08:08 Larkspur County Emergency Operations Center (EOC): the county shelter opens at Larkspur High School at 08:30 (220 cots, Red Cross staffing from 10:00). Large animals and recreational vehicles to the Juniper Springs Fairgrounds. Evacuees are asked to stay with family or friends outside the warning zone if they can.

'{unit_call} to net control: Bishop {bishop} unlocked the meetinghouse at {building} because cars with families from the south side were waiting in the parking lot in the rain. About twenty people inside now, more coming. Is this building a warming centre or not? Who decided?' (Operator: a work item with 'warming' in the title; the decision says which building opens, under whose authority and who runs it.)

need.label: The meetinghouse opened by the unit confirmed or redirected as a warming centre, with who decided and who runs it, within 30 minutes

injects.title: Stake President asks: which meetinghouse opens as the warming centre and staging point for families leaving the order zone? Recommendation within 30 minutes
injects.detail: Families are leaving with what they could carry. The county shelter at the high school opens at 08:30 but many members will come to a meetinghouse first. A building outside the warning zone, with power, parking and toilets; a building lead; a usage note for the facilities manager.
injects.next: ERD and specialist recommend one building and a lead; the Stake President decides; record the decision; tell the net

injects.note: One unit in the order zone reports two missionaries not accounted for.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control, priority: {unit} has two sister missionaries not accounted for. Their apartment is in the order zone near the creek; nobody answers the door; their phone goes to voicemail. Bishop {bishop} asks that the Stake President be told now.'
A Missionaries Not Accounted For alert should be on the EOC screens. Confirm it is owned, the Stake President has been told, and the call is logged as a note with the minute.

injects.title: Mission office asks: names, companionship and last known location of the missionaries not accounted for in {unit}
injects.detail: The mission office reached the EOC by phone before the lines jammed. They want the names, where the companionship was last seen, and who is looking.
injects.next: Get the names from Bishop {bishop}; reply to the mission office; log the time on the item
injects.note: Lands on the Work Items list (HIGH). Needs an owner and a logged reply.

need.label: Mission office answered with names and last known location within 30 minutes

injects.text: 08:20 Irrigation district to the county: the seep on the downstream face is now a flow the width of a road, carrying soil; a hole has opened on the crest. Failure is expected within the hour. Sheriff: everyone in the ORDER zone must be out now; deputies are going door to door below Route 30.

County amateur radio liaison: 'County channels are for agency traffic only. We will not relay family inquiries. Route your health-and-welfare traffic yourselves.' With {specialist}: decide where member-status and family inquiries go (the stake net and Winlink to the EOC address, never the county channel), who is net control and who succeeds them. Record it as a work item with 'health and welfare' in the title and the policy as its decision; have the net announce it.

need.label: Health-and-welfare traffic policy (path, net control, successor) recorded as a work item and announced within 25 minutes

injects.lesson: Helene 2024: the state would not accept inbound health-and-welfare traffic; spontaneous nets had no leader; Texas 2025: welfare messages moved by radio because circuits were overloaded.

injects.text: Many members in the south wards and the Spanish-language branch read Spanish first. The county alert and the stake net are in English. Decide with the bishops who sends the order, the warning and the meeting cancellation in Spanish, by which channels, and who answers Spanish callers at the warming centre. Record it as a work item with "Spanish" in the title and the plan as its decision.

need.label: Spanish-language notification and a Spanish speaker at the warming centre decided and recorded within 40 minutes

injects.lesson: Eaton and Palisades 2025: alerts and shelter information in English only left Spanish-speaking households behind.

injects.text: 08:28 Copper Creek Dam has failed. The reservoir is emptying through a breach in the embankment. Sheriff: the flood wave reaches Copper Ridge in about ten minutes, the south side of Larkspur in about thirty to forty, the Larkspur River bottoms and Alder Flat in about an hour and a half. Nobody goes back for belongings. Stay off Route 12 south of Center Street and Route 30 east of Larkspur.

Net control: 'All {stake} stations: the dam has failed. Stay out of the Copper Creek corridor and the river bottoms. Stations in the order zone, check in when you are out. No one goes back for belongings. Priority traffic only until further notice.'

08:32 Larkspur Regional Hospital (north Larkspur, above the water) is on normal power and taking patients; it asks that people with minor cuts and colds go to the warming centres, not the emergency room.

08:35 The flood wave reached Copper Ridge at 08:33. Water two metres deep is running across Route 30; the Route 30 bridge over Copper Creek at Copper Ridge was carried away at 08:36. Copper Ridge is cut in two: the wards south of the creek cannot reach the north bench by road. The Copper Ridge Retirement Village grounds are under water to the first-floor windows.

08:36 County: 911 is overloaded; calls hold for minutes or drop. Life-safety calls that cannot get through may be relayed in writing through the stake liaison to the county EOC: address, how many people and their condition, access route, call-back path. Do not promise a rescue.
injects.lesson: Helene 2024: 19 dispatch centres rerouted, one county dark for a month; Valencia 2024: the emergency number answered one call in five.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control, priority: a Team Leader reports a family of four on the garage roof at 2240 Willow Lane in {city}, water to the eaves, an elderly man among them with a heart condition. 911 is busy. Request relay to the county.' (Operator: a work item with 'roof' in the title; relay the address, people and condition, access (by boat from the north end of Willow Lane) and a call-back path through the liaison; the decision is the county's acknowledgement: call sign or name and the minute.)

need.role: EOC operator and the stake liaison to the county
need.label: Rooftop family in the unit relayed with address, people, access and call-back path; the county acknowledgement recorded as the decision within 20 minutes

injects.lesson: Helene 2024: the Mount Mitchell repeater carried medical coordination when 911 was dark.

injects.text: Larkspur County EOC: 'I can take one written message from your stake every 30 minutes: on the hour and the half hour. Put everything in it: life-safety relays, facilities, what you need from us.' Name the stake's liaison, batch the open life-safety and facilities items into one consolidated message, and send it on the next slot. Record it as a work item with 'liaison' in the title, the liaison's name and the message as its decision.

need.label: Stake liaison named and the first consolidated message to the county written for the next slot within 20 minutes

injects.lesson: Helene 2024: county emergency managers waited over an hour on saturated public-safety radio; one consolidated message per slot gets through.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control: with the Route 30 bridge gone, {unit} and the wards south of Copper Creek cannot reach the stake center. Bishop {bishop} asks the Stake President to open a Satellite EOC at the meetinghouse at {building}. It is above the water; we have a generator, a VHF station and a laptop.'

Decide whether a Satellite EOC opens at the meetinghouse at {building} for the wards south of Copper Creek, who leads it, and which wards report to it. Record the decision as a work item with "Satellite" in the title; have the net tell the wards the new Winlink address.

need.label: Satellite EOC south of the creek decided (lead, wards, Winlink address) and recorded within 30 minutes

injects.text: SITREP (situation report) #1: the first assessment goes as soon as possible. Generate it now from the reports on file (who has evacuated, missionaries, care-facility residents, warming centre) and send it up both lines: the coordinating council (Area Seventy) and the welfare line (WSRM, the Welfare and Self-Reliance Manager). Regular status reports follow on the interval leadership set on Setup.

'Juniper Springs station to net control: I have relatives in another state on the phone asking about three families in the south wards. Can I read the names on the net?' (Net control answers with the health-and-welfare policy, if there is one.)
SITREP #1 roll-up from {stake}
injects.note: Council / Area simulator only: one bundle per stake played by the simulator (no EOC laptop of its own), with every report due so far.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control: President {bishop} of {unit} reports that eleven of its families live in the order zone and several got the county alert in English only. Four families not reached. The branch needs the order and the warming-centre address in Spanish, read on the net and texted.' (Operator: a work item with 'Spanish' in the title, the families counted once on the branch's roster row, not again by the geographic wards.)

need.label: Spanish-language branch: the four families not reached are worked as one item, the message sent in Spanish, recorded within 45 minutes

injects.subject: Sandbag crews: River Road at Riverside

fields.type: Sandbag fill and placement crews with shovels, gloves and rain gear
fields.item: The Larkspur River will crest about 10:30 with the breach water on top of the snowmelt. Build a sandbag wall along River Road from Center Street to 1100 South to protect the sewer lift station and about thirty homes. The city has sand, bags and a loader at the River Road yard.
fields.deliver_to: River Road yard at 900 South; the crew leader checks in at Fire Station 1 first
fields.substitutes: Any able adults with shovels and rain gear; no one in moving water

need.label: The city's sandbag request owned within 15 minutes; crews with a leader and the safety acknowledgment decided and answered by ICS 213 within 45

injects.subject: Door-to-door accountability on the north bench

fields.item: The city has a list of 140 residents of the north bench who registered as needing help to evacuate. Teams of two to knock on doors, record who is home, who left and who needs a ride, and report to the fire station by radio. North bench only: nobody crosses toward the creek.
fields.deliver_to: Copper Ridge Fire Station, Route 30; lists and street assignments there
fields.substitutes: Any adults with a charged phone or FRS radio

need.label: Copper Ridge city's accountability request owned within 15 minutes; teams decided and answered by ICS 213 within 45

injects.text: 09:00 The flood wave reached the south side of Larkspur at 09:00. Water is over the Route 12 bridge over Copper Creek and the bridge is closed. Streets south of 500 South are under 30 to 120 cm of moving water. The Larkspur Care Center is surrounded by about 60 cm of water. Route 12 south of Larkspur is cut: Alder Flat is reached only by River Road on the west bank.

09:05 The Copper Creek electrical substation flooded at 09:05. Power is out across the south half of the valley: Larkspur south of Center Street, Copper Ridge and Alder Flat. Traffic lights are dark on Route 12.

Two attempts to reach the EOC by cell and text have failed in the last 15 minutes (09:02 and 09:08) and the fibre under the Route 12 bridge over Copper Creek is reported cut. Recommend to the Stake President that the stake go to CONTINGENCY (radio: Winlink VARA FM for forms, then VARA HF; FRS/GMRS and the stake net for voice).

09:08 Carrier notice: the fibre crossing under the Route 12 bridge over Copper Creek is cut and cell sites in the south half of the valley are on short battery or off the air. Calls and texts from Larkspur south of Center Street, Copper Ridge and Alder Flat are failing.

Decide the PACE level (Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency) on the recommendation of {specialist}. You decide; the specialist recommends; {erd} or the specialist announces it on the net. Then the EOC sets PACE on Setup.

Net control: 'All {stake} stations: by decision of the Stake President the stake is at CONTINGENCY as of 09:11. Disaster Reports, Supply Orders and Work Crew Logs go by Winlink VARA FM to {eoc_winlink}; VARA HF if you cannot reach a gateway. Voice traffic on this net and FRS/GMRS. Where there is no radio, send a runner with the paper form.'

At Contingency the EOC lives on its work items. Sort the list by priority; make sure every HIGH item (missionaries, life safety, care-facility transport) has an owner; set the Supply Orders and any Church-headquarters-assistance items to UP before the next SITREP.

injects.title: County EOC asks: how many people are in Church warming centres and how many member homes are flooded, by 10:00
injects.detail: Larkspur County EOC liaison: headcount at each meetinghouse in use and the number of member homes with water inside, by ward. Two numbers, not adjectives.
injects.next: Compile from the Disaster Reports and the warming-centre counts; reply through the county liaison on the next slot
injects.note: A request from the side, not the line above: answered from the reports on file.

need.label: County headcount answered within 45 minutes

injects.note: Supply Order for the care-facility residents moved to a building outside the warning zone.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control: a Team Leader reports the family at 415 Alder Street in {unit} not at home, car gone, not at the warming centre, nobody answers their phone. Requesting they be listed as not accounted for.' (Operator: one work item for the household, 'Alder Street' in the title.)

need.label: The household at 415 Alder Street in the unit logged as ONE work item and closed when they are found

injects.lesson: Helene 2024: the same homes were checked three to four times; missing lists fell by an order of magnitude on verification in Buncombe, Valencia, Kerr County and Lahaina.

injects.note: EMERGENCY path: the ward whose HAM operator lives in the flooded zone sends its update with a runner on foot; the operator types the paper form in.

injects.text: A runner hands the EOC a note from the Stake President's phone, which had one bar for a minute: 'Relatives in another state ask about the family at 415 Alder Street in {unit}; no answer since this morning. Please check.' (Same household, second path: add it to the open item, do not open another.)

Team Leader at the destination building: 'The residents of {unit} are here: I count them off the bus. The facility list says one more than I have. Staff think she left with her daughter at 08:10, but nobody wrote it down.' (EOC: the headcount at departure and arrival goes on the transport item; the one not seen is a life item until a person confirms where she is.)
injects.lesson: Eaton 2025: the roll call at the destination found two residents missing who had been assumed safe.

injects.note: Supply Orders from the flooded wards: water, cleaning kits, boots, gloves, pumps and wet/dry vacuums.

injects.text: 09:30 Nothing has been heard from {unit} since the cell sites went down. Its HAM operator lives in the flooded zone and its meetinghouse has no power. 'No report' is not 'no damage': flag it as a work item ('not heard from' in the title), ask the net for a relay or send a runner, and record the attempt as the decision.

need.label: The unit flagged as not heard from (a work item) within 10 minutes; a relay or runner attempt recorded as its decision

injects.lesson: Noto 2024: 33 districts isolated by road for days; Helene 2024: help went only where someone had asked.

injects.text: 09:34 Larkspur River at Center Street 3.9 m and rising, 70 cm over flood stage. Water is in the streets of the Riverside neighbourhood west of the river. The Center Street bridge stays open; the county watches it.

injects.note: The missing missionaries are found; follow-up Disaster Report from the same unit.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control: the two sister missionaries of {unit} are found, safe, at a member family's home in Juniper Springs. The family took them along at 07:55; their phone battery was dead. Bishop {bishop} asks the EOC to tell the mission office and clear the alert.'
injects.lesson: Reported missing is not verified missing: most people on early lists were safe with family.

injects.text: A member brings a satellite internet kit (Starlink) to the stake center. The building has no power on the south side but the generator runs the office. Before anyone calls the EOC "online": name an operator, a power source with its hours of fuel, a mount with open sky (it is raining and the roof is wet), then a round-trip test with the line above. Record it as a work item with "Starlink" in the title and those four answers as the decision.

need.label: Starlink set up with a named operator, power and hours, open sky and a round-trip test, recorded within 30 minutes

injects.lesson: Noto 2024: terminals sat unused for lack of anyone who knew how to run them; Helene 2024: terminals arrived days late without power.

injects.text: '{unit_call} to net control: {unit} reports 23 families from the south side staying with relatives in our ward boundaries. Names are with Bishop {bishop}. Please pass them to their home wards so they are marked accounted for and not searched for.' (Operator: a work item with 'staying with relatives' in the title; the decision says which home wards were told and by what path.)

need.label: Families staying with relatives in the unit passed to their home wards (verified, not reported missing) within 45 minutes

injects.lesson: Valencia, Kerr County and Lahaina: missing lists shrank by an order of magnitude once people staying with family were matched.

injects.subject: Crews to move belongings ahead of the river crest

fields.type: Moving crews of 4 with a pickup
fields.item: Residents in the warning zone west of the river (Riverside, 1100 South to 1600 South) asked for help to lift furniture and appliances to upper floors or carry them to trailers before the crest at about 10:30. Thirty-five homes on the city list. Stop at 10:15 or when the police close a street.
fields.deliver_to: Riverside Park parking lot; lists at the police command post
fields.substitutes: Any able adults; trailers and pickups welcome

need.label: The city's moving-crew request owned within 15 minutes; crews assigned, a stop time set and answered by ICS 213 within 40

injects.text: 'Repeater trustee to net control: the Saddleback Peak repeater lost commercial power with the substation and is on battery at 30 percent. The site generator needs fuel and the ridge road is mud. Expect to lose the repeater in about an hour. Stations in the south will need a simplex relay through a station on the north bench.' need.label: Relay plan for the south (station, frequency, who is told) recorded as a work item before the repeater dies

injects.lesson: Helene 2024: the backup repeater died when its batteries ran out and the generator failed; plan to run 72 hours with no communications.

injects.text: 09:52 The facilities manager reports 40 cm of water in the meetinghouse at {building} used by {unit}: carpets, the organ and the clerk's office on the floor. Nobody inside. Power off at the main. It is not a shelter and will need mud-out.

'Kestrel station to net control: several members say the Pine Hollow dam above Kestrel has failed too and the county has ordered all of Larkspur to evacuate. People are loading cars in the north wards. Can you confirm?' (EOC: a work item with 'Pine Hollow' in the title; check with the county before anything is relayed; the decision records the answer and the one correction sent under the Stake President's name.)

cards.text: Before T0: EOC (Emergency Operations Center) server and simulator running; a drill event open on the EOC with 'DRILL' in its name; the invented Juniper Plains pack loaded (check the privacy badge); on the Setup tab say what this simulator plays (a Stake EOC, a Satellite EOC's wards, or the councils of a Council / Area EOC) and which wards a satellite covers; every role player has their card and their device.
Several EOC laptops: every simulator on the same scenario and seed. Agree one start time and enter it on each Run tab (Schedule). Do not start until every EOC shows Ready.
Start the run. Read the opening narrative aloud: Sunday, rain, the dam seeping, an evacuation order. Do not say the dam will fail.
The dam fails. Read the breach note aloud. From here the clock matters: water reaches Copper Ridge at T+45, south Larkspur at T+70, Alder Flat at T+140.
Confirm the EOC header shows C (Contingency) after the Stake President's decision. If the players have not stepped down by T+85, ask the specialist what the triggers are.
Hand the paper form to the runner player for the ward with no HAM operator. Watch that the EOC types it in.
Hot wash from the checklist; then the after-action report (Hot wash tab): read the do-better list out by role and paste the text into the drill-feedback issue.

You are at home getting ready for church. Your phone works but calls fail one in three. {specialist} (Welfare and Self-Reliance Specialist, emergency communications) and {erd} (Emergency Response Director, ERD) will reach you.
Decide about the 9:00 meetings now: cancelled or not, which buildings, how members are told. You decide; the ERD or the specialist announces it.
The specialist will recommend how members in the order and warning zones are told. You decide the area, the action and the channels.
Missionaries not accounted for: direct the search and the call to the mission office; nothing goes up the line until the facts are known.
Decide on a Satellite EOC for the wards cut off by the lost bridge, and who leads it.
Decide the PACE level (Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency) on the specialist's recommendation; have it announced.

A meetinghouse shelters the public only with the Area's approval and a usage agreement. Ask; decide the interim plan; any correction of a rumour goes out once, under your name, after the county has confirmed.
Step up to Alternate only after three round-trip successes; later to Primary the same way, ward by ward.
Open the stake net on the Saddleback Peak repeater at T+6. Watch the Primary path: note the time of every failed call or text.
Recommend member notification to the Stake President: area, action, channels, languages. Log the minute.
Spanish: who sends the order and the meeting cancellation in Spanish, and who answers Spanish callers.
Two failed attempts in 15 minutes: recommend Contingency (Winlink VARA FM, then VARA HF; FRS and GMRS (Family and General Mobile Radio Service) and the net for voice).
The repeater is on battery: name a relay station and a simplex frequency before it dies, and tell the south.
Round-trip test before any step up. Three successes or no recommendation. Before calling Starlink "up": an operator, power with hours, open sky.
Get to the stake center. Your first jobs: the meetings decision with the Stake President, the warming-centre building, the care-facility transport.
Recommend one building as the warming centre: outside the warning zone, power, parking, toilets, a building lead. Record the decision.

City requests come by ICS 213RR (Incident Command System resource request). Own them within 15 minutes; answer by ICS 213 with crew leader, number and time. Crews need a team leader and the safety acknowledgment. No one goes into moving water.
Unasked volunteers and donated goods: hold, place with trained team leaders, or send home with thanks. Goods need a receiving site with an inventory owner, or a refusal and redirect.
Overnight: fuel, heat, dry clothes, cots, water per person. Quantities on the Supply Order; set it UP.
Write the 72-hour posture before the drill ends: shifts, fuel, paper rosters, a second laptop, mud-out tomorrow.
Your ward's families in the order zone must leave now. Use the ministering lists and the block captains. Who cannot leave on their own?
Send your first Disaster Report while the phones work: who has left, who is still home, who needs a ride, your missionaries.
Cell service is gone in the south. Reports go to your ward HAM operator for Winlink, or with a runner on paper.
Send an UPDATE report with corrected counts after the block checks. Report families staying with relatives as accounted for.
Knock on every door on your list in the order zone. Mark each household: left, staying, needs help. Do not enter moving water.
A household you cannot find: report it once, with the address. If you learn where they are, report that too, so nobody searches twice.
At the destination building, count the care-facility residents off the bus against the list. Report the count and any name not seen.

roles.title: HAM operator (ward station or net control)

cards.text: Net control opens the stake net on the Saddleback Peak repeater. Read the net cards as they come due.
Contingency: forms by Winlink VARA FM to the EOC address; VARA HF if no gateway answers. Short messages; the form tag carries the data.
Gateways congested: stop tests; life safety first, then the SITREP, then Supply Orders.
The repeater is gone: move to the relay frequency the EOC named.
Open the drill event; set the SITREP interval leadership gives you; watch the roster fill as first reports arrive by phone.
The Missionaries Not Accounted For alert: owned, the Stake President told, a note with the minute.
SITREP #1: first assessment as soon as possible, both lines above the stake.
Every HIGH item owned; Supply Orders and headquarters-assistance items set UP before the next SITREP.
SITREP #2: two numbers for members not accounted for (reported and verified); the six warming-centre figures.
If the Stake President opens you: tell your wards the new Winlink address; collect their reports; roll up to the Stake EOC on its interval, once, without double counting.
When the repeater fails you are on simplex or VARA HF. Keep paper copies of every report.

roles.title: Receiving stake EOC (north of the water)

cards.text: Families from the south are arriving at your meetinghouses. Ask the Stake President which building opens; do not let three buildings open by themselves.
Families staying with relatives in your wards: pass the names to their home wards so they are marked accounted for.
Order what your warming centre needs (cots, blankets, hygiene kits, food boxes, water) on one Supply Order, and log the crews that run it.

roles.title: Council / Area EOC (Juniper Springs Stake Center)

cards.text: Roll-ups arrive from the stakes without their own laptop. Merge them; answer the welfare line's totals request; send replies down.
The AWSRM (Area Welfare and Self-Reliance Manager) wants Supply Order totals by stake and the receiving building for each.
You approve Supply Orders that come UP. The truck is at Bramble Junction, 2.5 hours away; Route 12 from the south is cut.
Ask for a delivery point, a receiver and a route before the truck leaves. A "fulfilled" answer is not a delivery: ask for confirmation.
You have email only. Expect SITREP #1 when the stake has any internet; ask for it if it does not come.
The public-shelter request comes to you: approve under a usage agreement with the county, or say what the stake should do instead.
911 is overloaded. Accept life-safety relays in writing only: address, people and condition, access, call-back path.
One written message from each stake every 30 minutes, on the hour and half hour. Refuse family inquiries on county channels.
A donations truck nobody asked for wants a church to unload at. Ask the stake where it goes.

lessons_note: Injects marked "lesson" come from the research report docs/SIMULATOR_LESSONS.md (disasters of 2024 to 2026: Helene, Milton, the Los Angeles fires, Noto, Valencia, Kerr County and others). The lesson text is the evidence, in one line, for the hot wash. The places and people of this scenario are invented; the lessons are real.
agencies_note: Partner agencies that do not run this system (a city EOC) talk to the stake with the standard Winlink ICS forms: ICS 213RR to ask for resources, ICS 213 for messages and answers. Never a Church form. This invented scenario names its two city EOCs under "agencies" ({city_eoc} = Larkspur City EOC, SIM-LKCITY; {cr_city_eoc} = Copper Ridge City EOC, SIM-CRCITY); SIM- call signs are simulator stations, never on the air.
